j1r7Prep.independentRederivation: config, run packet and all five inputs byte-equal; command plans equal row by row; every residual difference listed
j1r7Prep.replay: the recorded J1-R6 outputs replayed through the J1-R7 validators: nine rows refused (boot check, three uploads, extract, verify, start, preflight, bundle); bootstrap, two uploads, health, identify, status and prove carry no package identity and were accepted structurally

reviews: Opus audits: RC9 ACCEPT; J1-R7 preparation ACCEPT (GO text items applied). The Fable 5.1 second opinion on the J1-R7 preparation agreed (0.8); its role-connection concern was checked by root against the source and is disclosed, not confirmed. A Fable 5.1 consistency check of the GO packet found 0 high, 1 medium and 5 low wording items; root confirmed and applied all six. Fable output is not acceptance evidence.
disclosures: the 11 suite cases have never run against any real PostgreSQL; the monitor SQL, the postmaster identity monitor and the du watchdog have never run while cases run
tasks may reach the unit limit of 32 or the job limit of 26 during the suite, and role connections are computed at 5 to 6 of 9 per phase but never observed; at a limit a case fails
a full suite makes start-once a silent SSH session of up to about 7 minutes and widens the prestart-to-postflight window to about 8-10 minutes, with one or two fallback timer fires
Node 24.21 does not gate network under the permission model (documented); the JavaScript socket guard is the only socket confinement
the bootstrap binder forbids only the A2 identity; a saved J1-R6 bootstrap output would fail closed at the first upload
the boot pin last matched at 2026-10-12 05:29 UTC; its current state is unknown
the J1-R6 and J1-R5 job bases, their inputs and the RC8 and RC7 package roots stay on the host
nextAction: Owner GO for one J1-R7 attempt; then root dispatches one Claude operations worker under the J1-R7 runbook.
